title: Choose the visual world for Localhost Recording Studio
question: The roll assigned Centre Label & Deadwax. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Centre Label & Deadwax
options.lineage: pressed records: liner notes, centre labels, run-out etchings
options.thesis: Every song is a pressing: the front stays bare, the details are etched in the deadwax.
options.viewport: The sleeve's back as the writing page: lyrics set large as liner notes, the style as one credit line, a gold centre-label button to cut the song; seed and steps live etched in a thin deadwax strip.
options.risk: Dark-with-gold can slide into the generic glowing-accent look if the label and etching aren't drawn with real restraint.

raised.raise: Every song carries the same fixed furniture: catalogue number, cut date, one-line style note.
Song structure drawn as a stepped rail, each section's height proportional to its length.
Gold is reserved for the one active thing: the song playing or the take being cut.
The centre label repeats at every scale, app icon to library row to now-playing, as one form.
The queue is a ruled list ranked by time; states restyle a row without moving the grid.

options.label: Lead Sheet
options.lineage: fake-book lead sheets handed to a session band
options.thesis: Write the song the way musicians hand it to a band: one page, sections boxed, nothing else.
options.viewport: One white page: boxed section marks [A] Verse, [B] Chorus beside the lyric lines, the style written as the tempo marking at top left, a single 'Record' action at the foot.
options.risk: Paper and notation is where many music tools land; it reads like notation software unless the chrome is stripped hard.

options.label: Catalogue Sleeve
options.lineage: post-punk label identity: catalogue numbers and pulse plots
options.thesis: Every song is a numbered catalogue entry whose face is a stacked plot of its own waveform.
options.viewport: LRS-014 as the only headline over a white-line pulse plot of the last song; the lyric field below in small engraved caps.
options.case: Fuses well: catalogue numbers and waveform plots suit songs; loses on clarity where colour codes replace titles.
options.risk: Cult reference; colour-coded names hurt scanability for newcomers.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.thesis: Queued songs as departures, ranked by time.
options.viewport: A board of queued renders with ETAs.
options.risk: Serves the queue only; writing gets no home.
options.case: Fuses poorly: songwriters don't identify with transit boards.
options.kept: The queue as a ruled list ranked by time.

options.label: Acetate Tab Manual
options.thesis: Sections as tabbed dividers with acetate leaves.
options.viewport: A tabbed manual page per song section.
options.case: Fuses poorly: wrong world for songwriting.
options.kept: Extent drawn as a stepped rail proportional to length.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: The song as a course over terrain.
options.kept: One reserved colour for the active leg only.

options.label: Bitmap Specimen
options.kept: One form repeated at every scale.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Songs as a ranked cast of characters.
options.viewport: A ranked grid of song characters.
options.kept: Fixed personal furniture under every item.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What AI music apps ship: a prompt box, a Create button, a grid of cover-art cards.
canonCard.viewport: A big prompt field with a gradient Create button above a feed of song cards with cover images.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
